# Policy Complexity Analysis (R-20)

Requirement R-20: "both the rule-based and (later) learned scheduling policies must be analyzable for computational complexity under the same input model." This document gives the Big-O statement for each policy's `decide()` call (derived from the code, not asserted) and measured wall-clock timing against real, identically-captured decision contexts -- the same input model for all three, per R-20's wording. Each figure is the mean over repeated calls against up to 5 real captured (FeatureVector, DecisionContext) pairs per config (fewer repetitions for the oracle, which is far more expensive per call -- see this module's docstring).

## Config config-a

| Policy | Big-O | Mean | Stdev | Min | Max | N |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | O(1) | 0.06 µs | 0.04 µs | 0.05 µs | 1.11 µs | 1000 |
| tree | O(depth), depth = MAX_DEPTH = 4 | 0.40 µs | 0.33 µs | 0.35 µs | 9.38 µs | 1000 |
| oracle | O(2 * horizon_ticks), horizon_ticks = ORACLE_HORIZON_S // dt_s = 90 | 12.588 ms | 122.90 µs | 12.406 ms | 12.844 ms | 25 |

The oracle is measured at ~31,130x the tree's mean decide() cost on this config, despite both being formally "constant" per decision point -- the constant factor (SGP4 propagation, FSM steps, and scheduler operations per rollout tick vs. a handful of float comparisons) dominates in practice. This is the concrete answer to "is the decision tree actually cheaper": yes, by several orders of magnitude, which is the real justification for using it in place of running the oracle onboard.

## Same-input benchmark (review rework, points 2.4/7.6)

Every policy is timed on the same 50 decision contexts, evenly spaced over all decision points of the 48 h seed-42 reference run under the always-serve baseline, with the same number of samples (50 contexts x 10 repetitions). One sample is the mean per-call time of 1000 back-to-back calls (baseline, tree) or of 1 call (lookahead, formerly "oracle") on one context. Host CPython timings; the baseline-FIFO and baseline-EDF variants share the same decide() (ordering is applied by the driver, not the policy), so one baseline row covers both.

### config-a

| Policy | Big-O | N samples | Median | p95 | Mean | Max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | O(1) | 500 | 0.02 µs | 0.02 µs | 0.02 µs | 0.03 µs |
| tree | O(depth), depth = MAX_DEPTH = 4 | 500 | 0.48 µs | 0.51 µs | 0.49 µs | 0.53 µs |
| lookahead ("oracle") | O(2 * horizon_ticks), horizon_ticks = ORACLE_HORIZON_S // dt_s = 90 | 500 | 8.509 ms | 10.015 ms | 8.602 ms | 11.152 ms |

### config-b

| Policy | Big-O | N samples | Median | p95 | Mean | Max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | O(1) | 500 | 0.02 µs | 0.02 µs | 0.02 µs | 0.03 µs |
| tree | O(depth), depth = MAX_DEPTH = 4 | 500 | 0.47 µs | 0.49 µs | 0.47 µs | 0.57 µs |
| lookahead ("oracle") | O(2 * horizon_ticks), horizon_ticks = ORACLE_HORIZON_S // dt_s = 90 | 500 | 8.674 ms | 10.191 ms | 8.637 ms | 10.791 ms |

**Tree on the MCU.** At most 4 float comparisons (MAX_DEPTH = 4); expected roughly 20-60 cycles including call overhead, i.e. under 1 us at 84 MHz on the Cortex-M4F. This is an estimate from instruction counts, not a measurement: the tree was never compiled for or run on the MCU.
